cases.request: Review an outbound client in a Java 25 / Spring Boot 4.1.1 service. The application injects RestClient.Builder elsewhere for tracing and TLS, but BillingClient uses RestClient.create(baseUrl). It POSTs /charges inside a loop that retries every RestClientException three times and creates a new Idempotency-Key each time. The provider sometimes records the charge and then the response is lost; the client reports a timeout. Operations says Boot timeout configuration has no effect and asks to add a typed @HttpExchange interface and keep the three retries. Propose the smallest correct implementation and test plan, including the timeout/response-loss outcome and any missing provider contract. Do not upgrade dependencies. No provider sandbox or runtime result is supplied.
criteria: Uses/configures the injected Boot-managed builder and builds interface proxy over that configured client, preserving customizers.
Checks resolved Boot/transport settings rather than blindly copying old property names; separates timeout surfaces and total attempt budget.
Treats POST timeout as unknown outcome, refuses blind redispatch/new-key-per-attempt and requires stable intent/idempotency/reconciliation contract.
Specifies actual loopback tests for request configuration, delayed/lost response and effect count, with execution honestly pending.

cases.request: Review a Java 17 source / Spring Security 7.1 Servlet resource server. NimbusJwtDecoder fetches an allowlisted JWKS URL. During issuer key rotation, a new kid arrives while JWKS is unavailable. The team proposes decoding the token without signature verification during the outage and trusting roles=[ADMIN] to permit edits to any requested account. Existing tests use jwt() and @WithMockUser only. Requirements: cached known-key tokens may continue under an agreed bounded freshness policy; unknown keys must not grant access; account edits must respect owner/tenant policy. Describe the implementation boundaries and executable negative tests. Also explain what changes if the product instead requires a removed key to stop being accepted immediately. Do not implement an identity provider or change the Java baseline.
criteria: Refuses decode-only fallback and rejects unknown key/unavailable verification without handler side effects.
Distinguishes cached known-key validation, rotation refresh and immediate revocation requirement; identifies bounded freshness/invalidation/introspection tradeoff.
Does not claim jwt()/WithMockUser prove decoder/JWKS/claim converter; specifies real signed tokens plus local HTTP and actual proxy.
Requires explicit type/allowlist authority mapping and object/tenant policy beyond ADMIN, preserving neighboring policy ownership and baseline.

cases.request: Review a Java 25 / Boot 4.1.1 test setup. @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment=RANDOM_PORT) is also @Transactional. A @BeforeEach repository.save creates an uncommitted account; a real HTTP POST tries to update it and emit an AFTER_COMMIT event. @AfterEach repository.deleteAll runs in the test transaction. The test asserts HTTP 200 but later suites observe leaked rows; another test uses a class-scoped container and a cached Spring context after that container stops. Docker is currently unavailable. Recommend focused changes and discriminating checks, while keeping real HTTP and after-commit behavior in scope. Report precisely which claims can be established without Docker.
criteria: Identifies server/test transaction separation and visibility of uncommitted setup; flush alone does not commit.
Requires committed setup and cleanup plus independent post-commit database/event observation, not only status200.
Aligns container/context lifetime without indiscriminate dirty-context masking; considers cache identity and disposal.
Distinguishes H2/local harness evidence from production engine/container execution and does not claim skipped/unexecuted tests passed.

cases.request: Review this Java 25 / Boot 4.1.1 workflow: CheckoutService.checkout() calls this.reserve() (reserve has @Transactional), saves an order, and publishes OrderAccepted. A listener has @Async plus @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT), calls a remote fulfillment service, then updates a local delivery marker. A developer says AFTER_COMMIT guarantees no event loss and exactly-once fulfillment. The process can stop after the database commit or after remote success before marking delivery. No XA transaction or provider deduplication contract exists. Propose concrete transaction boundaries and a recoverable implementation, with verification cases and explicit guarantees. Preserve independently committed order state during delivery failures.
criteria: Detects self-invocation transaction bypass and establishes real proxied/programmatic boundary plus rollback contract.
Explains after-commit/no-transaction/async limitations and rejects durable/exactly-once claims from annotation alone.
Makes event publication durable atomically with business commit and recovery/republication explicit, using outbox or appropriate persistent publication implementation.
Handles remote-success-before-marker as duplicate/unknown window, requires idempotency/reconciliation rather than exactly-once assertion; tests restart/failure and independent committed state.

cases.request: Review observability in Java 25 / Boot 4.1.1. HTTP endpoints already emit observations. A controller gets @Observed, calls an @Async service on a custom named ThreadPoolTaskExecutor, and adds userId, raw request URL and Authorization header to metric tags so every request is searchable. management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=* and a permitAll security chain are used for dashboards. Traces lose parent context in background work, and threads may be reused for another user. Propose scoped Boot wiring corrections and tests. There is no production collector/backend or load data; don't claim ingestion, privacy or overhead properties you cannot verify.
criteria: Inspects existing instrumentation to avoid duplicate observations; separates bounded metric dimensions from high-cardinality trace/log attributes and excludes secrets.
Configures/verifies propagation on actually selected custom executor including scope cleanup/no cross-task leakage; does not assume autoexecutor property configures every executor.
Narrows management exposure/access with explicit security and probe semantics, rather than all endpoints public.
Uses real Boot beans/async task boundaries and local observation/export evidence with parent/error/cleanup assertions; does not imply backend/load verification.

cases.request: Review migration wiring for a Java 25 / Spring Boot 4.1.1 app deploying 12 replicas to PostgreSQL. Flyway and Liquibase are both enabled, Hibernate ddl-auto=update, and there are application and reporting datasources; developers rely on @Primary to choose the migration target without checking. A deploy adds a mandatory column with existing rows while old app replicas still run. The proposal is to edit an already-applied migration and let every pod repair the checksum on startup. Choose a safe schema owner and Boot initialization plan, rollout/backfill order and failure/recovery checks. Explain startup migrations versus a separate migration job. Only H2 is available locally today; no PostgreSQL/container run has occurred.
criteria: Chooses one owner/runner per schema, removes competing Hibernate mutation and checks datasource/schema selection and initialization ordering.
Preserves applied migration history/checksums instead of automatic repair; versioned forward correction and explicit recovery evidence.
Plans expand/backfill/validation/enforcement/contract around old+new coexistence, not immediate destructive mandatory column.
Explains replica runner coordination and startup vs dedicated job tradeoff without claiming lock makes DDL online; distinguishes H2 wiring evidence from PostgreSQL rollout/locking proof.

Shared filesystem access is procedural, not a sandbox. Do not touch services, configuration, dependencies or source code. Write only response.md in your assigned temporary output directory using apply_patch, then report that path. You are not alone in the workspace; preserve others' files. limitations: These are proposals, not application implementations or application test executions by evaluation actors.
Shared filesystem isolation is procedural, not enforced sandboxing; actors were instructed to avoid other skills, rubrics and responses.
Known scenarios and teaching examples are not held-out evaluation; coordinator grading is not blinded; no statistical uplift is established.
Most without-skill responses already met all declared criteria; do not infer universal superiority from the few observed differences.
Migration criterion1 grading was corrected after runtime/pinned-source evidence; grade histories are retained in result records.
Actual automatic skill activation/routing in a client was not exercised.
One observability run was interrupted and replaced; one pre-fix testing run was retained and followed by a fresh final actor.
Java17 source compilation for security ran on Java25; Java17 runtime was not executed.

HTTP runtime coverage is the JDK imperative transport and interface proxy; WebClient, other transports, TLS, pooling/load, tracing, compressed bodies and persistent reconciliation are outside executed coverage.
Security does not establish discovery/TTL expiry, unknown-key aggregate flooding, connect/DNS/TLS stall behavior or transactional ownership-race safety.

Transaction recovery uses injected failure and orderly context/pool restart against an H2 file; it does not establish killed-process durability, replica races, broker delivery or exactly-once external effects.
Observability uses local meters and in-memory span capture; no production collector/backend, load cost, reactive or virtual-thread propagation was measured.
H2 migration and testing results do not establish PostgreSQL DDL, isolation, production rollout or actual release-binary compatibility.
Raw logs, snapshots and actor response files remain in local temporary directories; this repository record archives paths, decisions and source hashes, not those complete raw artifacts.
